1
Whether reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see
the Judgement.
2.     
To be referred to the Reporter or not.
Justice J.D. Kapoor (Oral)
1. On
account of having sold highly defective Generator Set on which respondent had
to incur heavy expenses to get it repaired, appellant vide impugned order dated
8.8.2007 passed by the District Forum
has been directed to pay Rs. 29,744/- which includes amount paid by the
respondent to Dilshad Electrical on 26.9.06 and compensation of Rs. 10,000/-
with Rs. 2000/- as cost of litigation.
2. Through
this appeal filed under
section 15
of
the C.P. Act the impugned order has been assailed on the premises that there
was no warranty for repairing of defects other
than engine failure and further
that this warrantee was international warranty and therefore the expenses
charged from the respondent for the
repairs done by the appellant were legally chargeable and appellant was not
liable to make payment of charges incurred by the respondent towards repairs
from the private electrician.
3.
In order to appreciate the aforesaid
contention of the learned counsel for the appellant, relevant facts leading to
the impugned order need to be stated in brief.
4. The
respondent purchased, being Director of M/s Neel Kanth Drugs (P) Ltd., one automatic voltage regulator (generator)
Element Honda Model 7600 DX from appellant on 8.5.2006 for a sum of Rs.
1,08,000/-. The product was sold with a warranty of one year. The generator
developed snag in August 2006. The respondent reported to appellant who alleged
that he had repaired it and charged a sum of Rs. 11,000/- on 3.8.2006 on the pretext that appellant will refund this amount on
reimbursement from the manufacturer of
generator. The generator again became defective within few days of first
repair. The appellant again charged Rs. 6,744/- on the old excuse. Hence
appellant charged Rs. 17,744/- from the respondent who is a bonafide consumer
for repairs within the warrantee on the false pretext that appellant would refund the amount on
reimbursement from the manufacturer of the generator. Inspite of payment of Rs. 17,744/- the
generator did not work well. The generator again became defective on 18.9.2006.
This time appellant refused to repair the generator. Appellant also refused to
refund a sum of Rs. 17,744/- charged by the appellant for repair on earlier
occasions. The respondent got the generator repaired from M/s Dilshad Electrical,
Shahdara and paid a sum Rs. 12000/- as repair charges. All expenses of Rs.
11,000/-, 6,717/- , Rs. 12000/- spent on the repair of generator were incurred
by respondent during the warranty
period. Consequently respondent filed the instant complaint before the
District Forum seeking refund of the expenses incurred during warranty 

 

period with cost and compensation.
5.
By contesting the claim of
the respondent, the appellant raised few legal objections as to the status of
the respondent as a consumer and the
generator having been purchased for commercial purpose which have been taken before the District Forum on merit, the appellant pleaded that no warranty
was ever issued to the respondent by
the appellant if at all it was issued it was the manufacturer of the generator set to
honour the warranty . It was pleased that the respondent damaged the generator
due to electrical overload put on the generator. Appellant did not deny the receipt of Rs. 17,744/- charged
by it.
6. We
have perused the impugned order and find that the District Form has relied upon
the copy of the invoice specifically
mentioning that there was one year warranty and also observed that even
otherwise every product is sold with implied
warranty of its quality for a reasonable period under the provisions of sales
of goods act. No seller can say that since warranty was not provided hence not responsible for
quality of product. Every seller is bound by implied
warranty under the provision of
Sales of
Goods Act
unless otherwise agreed in
writing.
7. The
international warranty being relied upon by the appellant is as under:-
The Honda General Purpose Engine installed on this OEM product
is covered by a Honda warranty, on the
following assumptions.
-
The warranty conditions
conform to those for the general-purpose engine established by Honda for each
country.
-
The warranty conditions
apply to engine failures caused by any manufacturing or specification problem.
-
The warranty deos not
apply to countries where there is no Honda distributor.
How to have your product
repaired under warranty:
Bring your OEM product to the
dealer who deals with Honda power products or the dealer who you purchased your
product form, with the receipt your received at the time of purchase as
evidence that your product is still under warranty. If the dealer judges that
the engine needs to be repaired warranty repair will be performed.
8. Even
if we accept the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the
defect repaired was not covered under the warranty period, still the appellant was
rightly directed to refund the cost of repairs. Any warranty or guarantee of
product or any goods is a promise to replace, remove the defect or any
part if some defects appeared during the
period of warranty. Any other kind of representation by way of warranty is misleading
and amounts to unfair trade practice.
9. Any
buyer or consumer who purchases a brand new article with minimum expectation that it will not cause
any inconvenience and discomfort to him at least during the period of warranty
and if the product develops defects within few days and continues to remain defective
and the consumer takes the article every now and then to the trader for
removing one defect or the other, the amount of
mental harassment, physical discomfort, financial loss is immense.
10. Quality of any goods
sold by a trader is tested on the anvil of definition of word
 defect provided by
Section 2(1)(f)
of
the consumer
Protection Act, 1986
which
means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity,
potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any
law for the time being in force. In such an eventuality there are four options
open to the Consumer Forum. First to
direct the trader to remove the
defect, second is to replace the goods
with new goods with same standard and
specification free from defect, third is
to refund the price to the consumer charged by the trader,
and fourth is to pay an amount as
compensation for any loss injury suffered by the consumer due to negligence of
the OP and fifth is to remove the
defects in goods or deficiencies in the services in question.
11. Invoice
and other documents placed on record
show that within short period, AVR was replaced by charging Rs. 11,000/-
from the respondent and further defect
was removed by charging Rs. 6,717/- . Generator further developed defects which
were not rectified by the appellant and respondent was forced to get it repaired
by private person on payment of Rs. 12,000/- .
12. In
terms of
section 14(1)(d)
every trader
is required to pay such amount as compensation
to the consumer for any loss or injuries
suffered by him due to the negligence of the OP. In the instant case, the respondent
has been compensated as to the actual loss suffered by him and has been
compensated as to the mental agony, harassment suffered by him which is his right as no person or any trader, service
provider who forces the consumer to seek
remedy by approaching legal forums can add insult to
injury, as
legal remedy is becoming costly
day by day and it involves an element of mental agony and torture as the adjudication of the cases takes years together .
13. Aforesaid
reasons persuade us to dismiss the
appeal.
14. Appeal
is dismissed in linine.
15. Impugned
order shall be complied with within one month after receipt of this order.
16.
 F.D.R./ Bank Guarantee,
if any, furnished by the appellant be returned forthwith after completion of
due formalities.
17.
 A copy of this order as
per statutory requirements, be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and
thereafter the file be consigned to the record room.
Announced on the Ist
May, 2008.
(Justice J.D.
Kapoor)
